questions.prompt: What does Copy-on-Write (CoW) do for Swift's `Array`, `Dictionary`, and `String`?

options.text: Shares the underlying buffer on assignment and only copies it when one copy is mutated while shared

questions.prompt: Why must a `struct` method that modifies `self` properties be marked `mutating`?

options.text: Value types are immutable by default inside methods; `mutating` allows reassigning `self` or its properties (and restricts calls to `var` instances)

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `map` and `compactMap` on a Swift collection?

options.text: `compactMap` transforms elements AND unwraps/drops `nil` results, returning `[U]` instead of `[U?]`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Swift closures. (Select all that apply.)

Non-escaping closures require `[weak self]` to avoid retain cycles
Trailing closure syntax lets you write `items.filter { $0 > 0 }` outside parentheses
Shorthand argument names `$0`, `$1` refer to positional parameters

questions.prompt: What does `Codable` (`typealias Codable = Encodable & Decodable`) enable in Swift?

options.text: Compiler-synthesized JSON/plist serialization and deserialization via `JSONEncoder` and `JSONDecoder`

questions.prompt: How do you map snake_case JSON keys (like `user_id`) to camelCase Swift properties (`userId`) without writing custom `CodingKeys`?
What does `protocol` + `extension` (Protocol-Oriented Programming) allow in Swift?

options.text: Providing default method implementations to all conforming types (including `struct`s and `enum`s)

questions.prompt: What does `defer { file.close() }` guarantee inside a Swift function?

options.text: Executes the `defer` block right before the current scope exits—whether via normal return, `guard`, or `throw`

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `try`, `try?`, and `try!`?

options.text: `try` propagates/catches errors in `do-catch`; `try?` converts a thrown error to `nil` (Optional); `try!` crashes if an error is thrown

questions.prompt: What does `Result<Data, NetworkError>` represent?

options.text: An enum with `.success(Data)` and `.failure(NetworkError)` for explicit typed error values

questions.prompt: Which Swift access level restricts a declaration to the *defining source file* only?
What is the difference between `public` and `open` for classes and methods in a Swift framework?

options.text: `open` allows modules outside the defining module to subclass/override; `public` allows use outside the module without subclassing/overriding

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Swift generics. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `where` clauses express multi-protocol or associated-type constraints cleanly
Generics are type-checked at compile time and specialized by the optimizer
Swift generics erase all types to `AnyObject` at compile time like Java
`func maxItem<T: Comparable>(_ a: T, _ b: T) -> T` constrains `T` to `Comparable`

questions.prompt: What does `associatedtype Item` inside a Swift `protocol Container` declare?

options.text: A placeholder type that each conforming type specifies (explicitly via `typealias` or via inference)

questions.prompt: What does `reduce(0, +)` do on `[1, 2, 3, 4]`?

options.text: Combines all elements starting from `0` using `+`, returning `10`

questions.prompt: What does `Self` (capital `S`) mean inside a protocol or class?

options.text: The concrete conforming type (or dynamic class type) itself

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `lazy` sequence operations (`nums.lazy.map(...).filter(...)`) and eager `nums.map(...).filter(...)`?

options.text: `lazy` avoids allocating intermediate arrays at each step, computing elements on demand during iteration

questions.prompt: Why must `Equatable` or `Hashable` synthesis include all stored properties (or implement custom `==` + `hash(into:)`)?

options.text: `Hashable` requires the invariant: if `a == b`, then `a.hashValue == b.hashValue`

questions.prompt: Match each Swift access modifier to its scope.

columns.label: Accessible anywhere within the same module/target
Accessible only within the enclosing declaration and same-file extensions

questions.prompt: What does `convenience init` on a Swift `class` do?

options.text: Defines a secondary initializer that MUST delegate to a designated `init` (`self.init(...)`) on the same class

questions.prompt: What does `required init` on a class require?

options.text: Every subclass must implement that initializer (often needed for `Codable` or `NSCoding` subclasses)

questions.prompt: What happens when `do { let x = try work() } catch MyError.timeout { ... } catch { ... }` runs?

options.text: `catch` without a pattern receives an implicit `error` constant

questions.prompt: What does `zip(names, scores)` return?

options.text: A sequence of `(name, score)` tuples stopping at the shorter of the two collections

questions.prompt: What does `@discardableResult` on a function suppress?

questions.prompt: What does `rethrows` on a higher-order function like `map` mean?

options.text: The function only throws if the closure argument passed to it throws—so callers with non-throwing closures don't need `try`

questions.prompt: What does `StaticString` represent compared to `String`?

options.text: A compile-time constant string literal known at compile time (used in `assert`, `precondition`, `fatalError`)

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `assert` and `precondition` in Swift?

options.text: `assert` is checked only in debug (`-Onone`) builds; `precondition` is checked in BOTH debug and release (`-O`) builds

questions.prompt: What does `Dictionary(grouping: users, by: \.role)` do?

options.text: Groups `users` into `[Role: [User]]` in a single pass

questions.prompt: What does `mutating` on an `enum` method allow?

options.text: Changing `self` to a different enum case (`self = .active`)

questions.prompt: What does `#if DEBUG` ... `#endif` do in Swift?

options.text: Conditional compilation directive excluding debug-only code from release builds

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `String` vs `Substring` in Swift. (Select all that apply.)
